metaDescription: Plevna, MT sits on the Cedar Creek Anticline, a Red River/Ratcliffe trend older than the Bakken. I buy mineral interests here based on real production history.
heroLead: Plevna sits on the Cedar Creek Anticline, and if your family's mineral history here goes back generations, it's probably a Cedar Creek story before it's ever a Bakken story.
intro: The Cedar Creek Anticline is one of the older structural oil trends in eastern Montana, producing out of the Red River and Ratcliffe zones since the 1950s and 60s, well before Bakken horizontal drilling ever reached this part of the state. Fallon County sits along that structure, and Plevna-area mineral interests are more likely tied to that older conventional history than to the newer unconventional play most people associate with Montana's oil counties today.

I bring this up early because it changes what I look for in the record. A Cedar Creek-era interest reads differently than a Bakken-era one, with its own leasing patterns, its own operators, and its own decline behavior, and I evaluate it on those terms rather than by comparing it to the newer play.

sections.heading: Reading an old Cedar Creek lease correctly
paragraphs: A lot of the leasing activity along this trend happened decades ago, with some wells still producing at low stripper rates and others long since plugged. I check whether your family's interest sits on ground with current production, expired leasehold, or somewhere in between, because those three situations are priced very differently.

sections.heading: Has any Bakken-era activity reached Plevna?
paragraphs: Some exploratory interest has touched Fallon County over the years, but it hasn't developed into the kind of sustained horizontal drilling seen further north in Richland County. I check current lease status and any recent permitting on your specific parcel rather than assuming Bakken-level activity applies here.

faqs.question: What is the Cedar Creek Anticline?
faqs.answer: An older structural oil trend running through eastern Montana, producing from the Red River and Ratcliffe formations since the 1950s and 60s, distinct from the newer Bakken play.

faqs.question: Is my family's old lease tied to Cedar Creek or the Bakken?
faqs.answer: Most likely Cedar Creek if it dates back several decades. I check the actual lease history to confirm.

faqs.question: Is there current production near Plevna?
faqs.answer: Some, at mature stripper-well rates on parts of the Cedar Creek trend. I check the status of your specific parcel before discussing value.

faqs.question: Where do you verify ownership for a Plevna-area parcel?
faqs.answer: Through the Fallon County Clerk and Recorder in Baker, where I pull the full deed chain before making an offer.
